head: claude/soak-alarm-threshold
title: MI-61: a soak must alarm — a threshold, a timer, and a state for a DEAD soak
body:
## Summary Implements the standing operator directive of 2026-09-02 — *"anything soaking needs to be logged with an alarm that has either a timer or a soak threshold, so that we know to get back to it when the soak is ready"* — as a binding rule, a register field, a four-state grader, a due-list source and a CI guard. It also files the register row for the Bybit graded-coverage soak, which was tracked nowhere. **Tier-1 throughout**: registers, tooling, CI, docs. No order path, no `config/`, no live-VM mutation, no secret. **DRAFT — please do not merge on my account.** --- ## ⚠️ First: two corrections to the brief I was given **RULE ONE — I checked rather than relaying.** Both corrections are in the direction that would have made this PR overstate itself. **1. `CLAUDE.md` does NOT claim `due-list.yml` has never fired on cron.** I was told it does and that fixing it was part of the job. It does not: `grep` for `due-list`, `cron` and `never fired` across `CLAUDE.md` returns nothing of the kind. The row that carried that claim — `OI-20260901-SCHEDULED-PROBES-AND-DUE-LIST-HAVE-NEVER-FIRED-ON-CRON` — was **already CLEARED on 2026-09-02** and is recorded as cleared in `OPEN-ITEMS.json`. What is genuinely stale is six *other* files that still cite it as a live row, and I corrected the one that was mine to take (`scripts/ops/work_digest.py`). `src/runtime/close_wedge_standing.py` turned out to already carry the correction. The four `.github/workflows/*.yml` headers are left to **MI-60**, which holds workflow territory — listed in my board `START` so they are not lost. **2. I could not reproduce the `event=schedule` measurement, and I am not claiming it as mine.** `api.github.com` is intercepted from this sandbox — HTTP 403 with a Claude-specific body, exactly as `scripts/ops/probe_actions_log.py` documents. I tried it and got that 403. **What I could check is in-repo and independent**, because `due-list.yml` commits its own output to `main`, so its firings leave a trace in git history: | commit | landed | declared cron | late by | |---|---|---|---| | `50722d1e` | 2026-09-01T10:31:01Z | `50 5 * * *` (05:50 UTC) | **4h41m** | | `f292f7a9` | 2026-09-02T09:57:37Z | `50 5 * * *` (05:50 UTC) | **4h07m** | **23h27m apart.** So it fires — *roughly* daily, and **erratically**. "It fires" is not "it fires on time", and that is the honest ceiling on this work: the alarm rides the due-list, so what is on offer is surfacing within ~4–5 hours of an unpredictable offset, not same-day delivery. ⚠️ Note what the git evidence does **not** establish: a commit proves the workflow ran and committed, not that the trigger was `schedule` rather than a `workflow_dispatch`. Two independent sources agreeing on the timestamps is why I state it; one of them being unreachable from here is why I label it. --- ## The gap, measured before building - **All 36 `monitoring` rows were TIMER-ONLY.** `check_every_days` says how often a human must LOOK; **no field anywhere could say what it is looking FOR.** A soak that went ready on day 2 waited for its day-3 cadence; a soak that had DIED on day 1 was re-checked on that cadence forever with nothing to find. - **Of 12 `*_soak.jsonl` logs declared in `src/`, only 4 were named anywhere in the register** — and only in a *probe command*, which is a reader, not an alarm. **Eight accrued to nobody.** (The guard's own detector, which is broader, counts **16**, of which **zero** carried an alarm.) - **`bybit_coverage_soak` (#10746) had no row at all.** Its PR proposes a *health-review-backlog* row, and the backlog is **not** a due-list source — `render_due_list.py::SOURCES` reads `open_items`, `operator_owed`, `research_queue`, `probes`, `red_crons`, `unlanded_automation`. So the only declared evidence for widening a gate toward **real-money `bybit_2`** would have accrued, or failed to accrue, and surfaced to nobody. --- ## What this builds **1. The missing row, filed FIRST** (`8486f6ad`, before any schema work, so it could not be lost if the rest were cut). Its criterion is a field value, not elapsed time: a row carrying `verdicts_differ: true`, per MI-49's explicit bar that time and quiet do not count. It records the two ways it must not be misread — an empty log is *expected* while arming is held, and the soak **may legitimately never go ready**, in which case the honest report is *"unproven"*, not *"proven-good"*. **2. The collapse, fixed where it physically lived** (`630e6bdb`). `probe_lib.report()` returned `EXIT_FAIL` for **both** *0-of-0 rows* and *0-of-8,520 rows*. Its own docstring says those are different findings, and the branch printed *"A ZERO DENOMINATOR IS NOT A NEGATIVE"* — then returned the same code, so `run_probes.py` recorded one state and nothing downstream could act on it. The prose was right and unreachable; field beats comment, and here the field was wrong. Now `EXIT_SOURCE_EMPTY = 3` → `run_probes` state `source_empty`, plus machine-readable `matched`/`scanned` counts. **3. The grader** — `scripts/ops/soak_alarm.py`. Four states, never collapsed: | state | meaning | surfaces | |---|---|---| | `ready` | threshold MET — come back now | **loud row** | | `not_writing` | **NO rows since declared — the soak is DEAD** | **loud row** | | `unknown` | we could not READ the file | quiet row | | `accruing` | rows arriving, threshold not met | **no row** — context only | **4. The due-list reads it** — `render_due_list.py::src_soaks`, plus a `soak` block on the register: `{log, declared_at, ready_when, min_matching}`. A block with no `ready_when` is **refused** (it would be a second timer wearing a threshold's name); with no `declared_at` it is refused too (*"no rows since it was declared"* has no meaning without a start date); `min_matching: 0` is refused as decorative. **5. The rule + the guard** — `docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` § *"A soak must carry its own alarm"*, and `scripts/ci/check_soak_registered.py` (`soak-registered-guard`, every PR). --- ## ⚠️ The alarm-fatigue refusal, which is the load-bearing design decision **`accruing` produces no row, and this PR REMOVES a daily page rather than only adding new ones.** `src_probes` emits a **LOUD** due row for every probe in state `fail` — and before this change a patiently-accruing soak **was** `fail`. So a healthy soak was already firing a loud row every single day, inside the machinery built to prevent exactly that. `src_probes` now defers every soak-declaring row to `src_soaks` and **states the hand-off in its note**, so it can never be silent. An unreadable register defers nothing: the fail-safe direction is to keep reporting a probe fail, never to lose a signal. This is the P1 this repo has already paid for — `BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN-RESETS-ON-EVERY-RESTART` put **one** un-latched condition on **53.7% of the operator's entire ERROR+ feed**. --- ## Test plan - [x] `soak_alarm.py` — **28 planted controls**, including one test per state proving `not_writing` is reachable and distinguishable from `accruing` **and** from `unknown`, and that a `fail` with *no counts* stays `accruing` (coercing a missing denominator to 0 is exactly how an unread probe manufactures a false dead-soak alarm). - [x] `render_due_list.py` — **26 → 40 controls**, asserting the *rendered output*: which verdicts become rows, which become loud, and that `accruing` becomes none. - [x] `probe_lib.py` 25 → **37**, `run_probes.py` 20 → **22**, `probe_soak.py` 3 → **4**. The control that would have FAILED before this change asserts `rc(0-of-0) != rc(0-of-N)`; both were `EXIT_FAIL` and the old controls compared only printed text. - [x] `check_soak_registered.py` — **11 controls**, including the planted **positive** (a new unregistered soak MUST fail): a guard that has only ever reported clean is indistinguishable from one that scans nothing. - [x] **Rendered, not just unit-tested.** All four states pushed through the real renderer against a fixture root — `ready` and `not_writing` appear in `DUE.md` with 🔔, `unknown` without it, `accruing` in no row and in the note as *"accruing (not surfaced, healthy)"*. Output below. - [x] **The guard proven against the real case**: dropped #10746's actual `bybit_coverage_soak.py` into the tree. With my register row it passes (17 declared, 1 registered); with the `soak` block removed it **FAILS**, naming `bybit_coverage_soak` and the fix. - [x] `due-list --check` OK · `open-items-guard` OK (37 items) · `probes --check` OK · `ruff check .` clean · `check_backlog_refs` OK. - [ ] CI green
The actual DUE.md render — all four states ``` - 🔔 **OI-DEAD** (soaks · 13d) — soak NOT_WRITING — ⚠️ THE SOAK HAS WRITTEN NOTHING — 13d since it was declared on 2026-08-20. The log was READ successfully and held ZERO rows, so this is a measurement, not a failure to look. Waiting longer cannot help: either the writer is not deployed, not armed, or broken. - 🔔 **OI-READY** (soaks · 13d) — soak READY — ✅ READY — 2 matching row(s) of 631 scanned satisfy the declared criterion (verdicts_differ=true). ⚠️ Ready is not CLEARED: read the row's `clears_when`. - **OI-UNREADABLE** (soaks · 13d) — soak UNKNOWN — the probe COULD NOT READ the soak — this says nothing about whether rows exist. ⚠️ It is NOT `not_writing`: an unreadable log and an empty log are opposite findings. soaks source note: 4 declared soak(s): ready=1 · accruing=1 · not_writing=1 · unknown=1 | accruing (not surfaced, healthy): OI-ACCRUING: accruing ```
--- ## ⚠️ What remains UNPROVEN — do not read a green CI as the done-condition **The done-condition is a real soak row crossing its threshold and the item appearing as due. That has not happened, and nothing here shows it has.** 1. **No soak has ever gone `ready` on real data.** Every `ready` and `not_writing` verdict demonstrated above came from a fixture. The mechanism is exercised; the *phenomenon* is not. 2. **The one real declared soak grades `unknown` today** — correctly. `bybit_coverage_soak` has no probe, because #10746 is unmerged, the gate is unarmed, and there is no row yet to serve as a positive control. So on the live tree this ships **surfacing one quiet row that says nobody is looking**. That is the honest state, not a working alarm. 3. **`not_writing` has never fired on a real log.** Its first genuine test is after #10746 merges *and* the arm is read back off `/proc//environ`. Until then an empty log is correct-by-design and the row says so. 4. **The cadence is erratic** (measured above, 4h07m–4h41m late). An alarm on this carrier is not same-day. 5. **CI green proves none of the above.** A green suite over a path the suite does not exercise is not evidence about that path. 6. **The guard's escape hatch is real and stated**: adding a name to `BASELINE` is cheaper than writing a register row. It is not *silent* — the name is a visible line in the PR diff under a comment saying the list may only shrink, the guard fails on a `BASELINE` entry whose writer is gone, and it prints the debt count on every run. That is the difference from `new-table-wiring-guard`. It is not a proof of good faith. 7. **16 soak logs remain unregistered**, carried as dated debt. This PR makes that number visible and countable on every CI run; it does not reduce it. ## Filed for follow-ups - The **16 baselined soaks** each need a real register row. Deliberately out of scope: writing 16 `ready_when` criteria I cannot verify would be exactly the decorative declaration the guard refuses. - The four `.github/workflows/*.yml` headers still citing the cleared cron row — **MI-60's territory**, flagged on the board rather than contended for. - Once #10746 merges and `bybit_1` is armed, that row's `probe_absent_reason` should be **replaced, not re-affirmed**: the probe is a one-liner (`probe_soak.py --path '…name=bybit_coverage_soak&lines=1000' --require verdicts_differ=true --positive-control account_id=bybit_1`). A buildable gap left wearing the label of a permanent one is the error `probe_api.py` was written to correct. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01NfzmaV7FxP4bAZtKbXYVb9
